newsitem.title: UK: London stocks end lower as Wall St worries weigh.
newsitem.headline: London stocks end lower as Wall St worries weigh.

text.p: UK shares finished moderately lower on Tuesday as investors remained nervous about a possible Wall Street slide after its recent weakness.
Although the Dow has dropped five percent since hitting an all-time peak last month, many market participants believe U.S. blue chips are due for a more substantial correction.
"People are looking for excuses to sell this market not to buy it," the head of trading at a large brokerage said.
"The Dow looks like it's headed lower. It really depends now on how much we (FTSE) follow it."
The FTSE 100 index ended 14.2 points down at 3,979.6.
The Dow, which dropped 30 points in the first few minutes of trade on Tuesday, was down five points by the London close.
Strategists expect the Dow and the FTSE to suffer further turbulence in the coming weeks as investors fret about higher U.S. interest rates in the New Year.
Fears of higher rates were heightened after news that U.S. housing starts had risen to their highest levels since July last year, taking economists by surprise.
Although the U.S. Federal Reserve is not expected to move on interest rates after today's regular monetary meeting, some economists fear a rate hike could come early next year.

"Bond yields are pushing up. If there are further signs that the U.S. economy is picking up fueling price pressures, we could see the Fed move in February," said Kirit Shah, strategist at Sanwa International.
Such an event would put Wall Street under pressure as yields on U.S. treasury bonds increased, Shah said.
"Dow weakness will inevitably have an impact on the FTSE, although I don't think we'll have as big a shake out as in the U.S."
Over the next few weeks Shah expects the FTSE to remain trapped in a narrow range of 3,900 to 4,050.
"The FTSE has pretty good support at 3,900. I wouldn't look for it to slip much below that point," he said.
Overall market pessimism towards equities was heightened after Morgan Stanley recommended reducing stock holdings.
The U.S. investment bank changed its global asset allocation to 56 percent stocks, 29 percent bonds and 15 percent cash versus an original 74 percent stock and 26 percent bonds bias.
British Aerospace flew against the downward market draft, climbing 19p to 11.55-1/2 stg amid hopes that the Boeing merger with McDonnell Douglas would ultimately prove favourable for the UK group.
Insurance stocks were also generally higher as Monday's merger agreement between insurance brokers JIB Group and Lloyd Thompson fanned bid speculation around the sector.
Commercial Union rose 11-1/2 at 691-1/2 after briefly touching a 1996 high of 696p while General Accident gained 21p at 716-1/2.
Severn Trent added 15p to 669 after news the water company had instructed a broker to buy back up to 18 million of its share, representing five percent of the group's share capital.

British Gas was one of the most active of the FTSE 100, easing 5-1/2p to 223-1/2 after analysts at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, the company's broker, reduced the stock to "hold" from "buy" and lowered dividend forecasts for next year.
Trading volume in British Gas was 12.7 million by 1630 GMT.
Pearson dropped 14p at 687 after cautious press comment ahead of a trading statement from the media and leisure group on Wednesday. Dealers expect the statement before trading tomorrow.
UK gilts ended lower, unsettled by the weaker U.S. treasuries market. The March long gilt future closed 12/32 lower at 108-22/32.
-- Dale Faulken, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
